correctness.rationale: For v>b both internal-state velocities have fixed opposing signs everywhere. Zero total stationary flux forces p_+=(v-f)P/(2v) and p_-=(v+f)P/(2v). The scalar flux equation has rate L in each f=+b segment and -R in each f=-b segment; cusp interface flux continuity yields the unique piecewise exponential invariant density. Tail integrability is exactly L,R>0. Half-line integrals give M_+ as ratio of two exponentially large peak terms; the omitted normalization terms are exponentially small, and a(L-R)=theta(1+epsilon/(2b+epsilon)) gives the claimed uniform Taylor coefficient. Conditional changes x=±a+epsilon y yield Laplace densities in L1 and orientation mismatch equals epsilon/(2v) exactly. All boundaries v>b, alpha±>0 and fixed theta are explicit. The standalone checker passed 125 tests but is supporting, not a proof.

value.rationale: The force threshold v=b is a natural physical and mathematical singular boundary where one propagation velocity vanishes. The result exactly identifies the unique weak-bias scale that competes with that singularity, a universal nontrivial interpolation from 0 to 1 in well-selection probability, independent Laplace-scale local fluctuations and orientation locking. The first correction unexpectedly depends on force slope but not the mean flip rate. These are motivated collective structural consequences rather than isolated numerical parameter values; the statement explicitly excludes noise and mixing-time claims.
